ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, objects A and B are connected through a thin string and a light spring on the two sides of a light pulley fixed on the ceiling. The masses of objects A and B are both m. At the beginning, the thin string is straight; object A is held by hand so that the spring is at its original length and the distance between A and the ground is h, while object B is at rest on the ground. After letting go, object A falls, and when it is about to contact the ground, the magnitude of its velocity is v. At this time, object B happens to exert no pressure on the ground. Then which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The stiffness coefficient of the spring is mg/h

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, above is a light pulley fixed on the ceiling, and the thin rope passes over the pulley. The left rope end vertically downward connects to object B, and B is placed on the ground; the right rope end vertically downward connects to a light spring, and the lower end of the spring connects to object A. Object A is above the ground, and the vertical distance from A to the ground is marked as h in the figure. Reasoning: When A falls to the point of being about to contact the ground, the problem statement says that B happens to exert no pressure on the ground; this is the critical state in which B is about to leave the ground. At this time B is subjected to gravity mg downward and the rope tension T upward, and the supporting force of the ground on B is 0, so T=mg. The light rope and light pulley make the tension in the rope equal to the tension received by the upper end of the spring on the right side, and the magnitude of the elastic force transmitted by the light spring is also T. Since B is still on the ground before this critical moment, the length of the left end of the rope is unchanged, the pulley is fixed, and the rope is inextensible, so the position of the upper end of the spring on the right side is unchanged. Initially the spring is at its original length; A falls from a height h above the ground to being about to touch the ground, and the lower end of the spring descends h with A, so the elongation of the spring is x=h. By Hooke's law T=kx, obtain mg=k h, so k=mg/h. The velocity v in the problem does not affect this result.
